card.name: Shota
card.era: Traditional; stage form codified mid-20th c. (Pristina Shota ensemble founded 1948)
card.tagline: Flirtatious Kosovar couple's dance with handkerchiefs and quick footwork.
card.profile: Shota (also Vallja e Shotës) is an Albanian dance from northern Albania and Kosovo: an idyllic, flirtatious duet for a girl and a boy who move around each other without touching, with intricate arm gestures, synchronized steps and a strong 2/4 rhythm, ending with the exchange of a scarf. Commonly performed at weddings and folk festivals, its modern stage choreography originated with the professional Shota ensemble of Pristina and was adopted by the Yugoslav ensembles Kolo and Tanec (English Wikipedia; albanian-folklore.com).
card.insight: Widely recognized as the symbol of Kosovo folklore and an emblem of Albanian patriotism; its name is popularly but disputedly linked to the heroine Shote Galica, while folklorists trace 'Vallja e shotës' to a folk term for the wild duck whose mating display the movements evoke (English Wikipedia; albanian-folklore.com).
card.image_significance: Flirtatious 'wild-duck' courtship duet. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — N. Albania/Kosovo, Albania/Kosovo.
